title: Choose Pesoprint's visual world: full steampunk
question: Round 3, steered to brass, gears, gauges, rivets and machinery. The roll assigned The Locomotive Works. Keep it, take my pick, or re-roll.

options.label: The Locomotive Works
options.lineage: Victorian locomotive works: riveted boiler plate, lined-out livery panels, cast brass works plates, and the brass gauges of the cab
options.thesis: Every model leaves the works with its own number plate, and the cab gauges read out its price and print time.
materials: cast brass works plates and gauges
options.viewport: A riveted crimson livery panel with brass beading. The headline sits left, with three cast-brass levers (Free / File / Print). On the right is a porthole holding the object, a meshing gear train, and two brass gauges reading price and print time.
options.risk: Plenty of steampunk, so the danger is clutter. The buying panel must stay calm and legible, and the gauges must show real values, not ornament.

raised.raise: One calm panel: among the brass and rivets, the buying panel is a plain enamel-white plate with nothing decorative inside it.
Buffer-beam stripes only on actions: the red-and-black hazard stripe marks the primary action and nothing else.
Works numbers: every model has a number plate and can be found by it (Works No. 014).
One active edge: a single bright brass line marks the selected option. Everything else stays dull brass.
Crop hard: product photos fill their porthole or plate edge to edge.
A fixed livery: four paint colours plus brass, with no tints or in-between shades.

options.label: The Engine Room
options.lineage: steamship engine rooms: brass pressure gauges, valve wheels, copper pipework, and the engine-order telegraph
options.thesis: You set the order on a brass engine-order telegraph (Free, File or Print), and the engine room answers.
options.viewport: A large brass engine-order telegraph dominates the right, its lever set to PRINT. Copper pipes run along the top with gauges, and the headline and search sit left on dark teal steel.
options.risk: Familiar: gauges and copper pipes are steampunk's stock image, so it may read as a theme park more than a shop.

options.label: Industrial Quote Streetwear
options.thesis: Ordinary words in quotes, hazard stripes, zip-tie tags.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Blocks of weather cut and assembled.
options.case: No link to machinery or objects.

options.label: Teletext
options.thesis: The catalogue as numbered teletext pages.
options.case: Retro, but electronic, not steampunk, and it can't show objects.

options.label: Riso Web System
options.case: Already declined once; it hides true colour.
options.kept: A fixed palette with no tints.

options.label: Festival Hoarding
options.thesis: Layered flyers, one calm white panel.
options.viewport: Busy collage with one ticket panel.
options.case: Loud but not steampunk; no photography.
options.kept: One calm panel amid the noise.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A 3D-model site like the big repositories, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A search-led header, category chips, and rows of model cards with price and download badges.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other model repository by design.
